levels_of_evidence.description: Data derived from multiple randomized clinical trials or meta-analyses.
Data derived from a single randomized clinical trial or large non-randomized studies.
Consensus of opinion of the experts and/or small studies, retrospective studies, registries.

content.declaration_of_interest: The experts of the writing and reviewing panels provided declaration of interest forms for all relationships that might be perceived as real or potential sources of conflicts of interest. Declarations were reviewed according to the ESC declaration of interest rules and can be found on the ESC website (http://www.escardio.org/guidelines). Declarations have been compiled in a report and published in a supplementary document simultaneously to the guidelines.
content.transparency_and_conflict_management: This process ensures transparency and prevents potential biases in development and review. Any changes in declarations during the writing period were notified to the ESC and updated. The Task Force received its entire financial support from the ESC without involvement from the healthcare industry.
content.guideline_development_and_endorsement: The ESC CPG supervises and coordinates preparation of new guidelines and is responsible for endorsement. ESC Guidelines undergo extensive review by the CPG and external experts. After revisions, guidelines are signed off by all experts in the Task Force and the finalized document is signed-off by the CPG for publication in the European Heart Journal (EHJ). Guidelines were developed after careful consideration of scientific and medical knowledge and evidence available at the time.
content.educational_tools_and_implementation: Development of ESC Guidelines includes creating educational tools and implementation programmes: condensed pocket guideline versions, summary slides, summary cards for non-specialists, and electronic versions for digital applications (smartphones, etc.). These are abridged; users should access the full text via the ESC website and EHJ. National Cardiac Societies are encouraged to endorse, adopt, translate and implement ESC Guidelines. Implementation programmes are needed because outcomes may be favorably influenced by thorough application of clinical recommendations.
